      - line „Twój adres: ” + TextLink `https://dev.architektow3d.pl/<wbr>{handle}`, `--type-sm` muted, `overflow-wrap: anywhere`;
      - form column, gap 16 px: FormField label „Adres profilu”, hint „Od 3 do 30 znaków: małe litery, cyfry i myślniki.”, status „To jest Twój obecny adres.” while unchanged, error = the hint text while invalid;
      - inside the field: Input `mono` (no prefix) + a `--type-mono` `--text-subtle` preview line `{origin}<wbr>{handle}`;
      - success `StatusMessage tone="success"` „Adres zmieniony. Stary adres przekierowuje przez 30 dni.”;
      - `Button` (size `md`) „Zmień adres”, `align-self: flex-start`, disabled when unchanged or invalid.

      FormField order here is input → preview → error/status → hint (design/components/forms/FormField.jsx:11-20); today it is input → preview → hint → feedback (`src/app/[locale]/(app)/handle-form.tsx:380-401`).
   4. Password (design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:94-102): „Bieżące hasło”, „Nowe hasło” with hint „Od 8 do 128 znaków — bez żadnych dodatkowych wymagań.”, success `StatusMessage tone="success"` „Hasło zmienione. Pozostałe urządzenia zostały wylogowane.”, `Button` „Zmień hasło”.
   5. E-mail (design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:105-120):
      - form: „Nowy adres e-mail” (error „Podaj poprawny adres e-mail.”), `Button` „Wyślij link potwierdzający”;
      - sent: column gap 16 px with `StatusMessage tone="info"` „Jeśli ten adres jest wolny, wysłaliśmy na niego link potwierdzający (ważny 24 godziny). Nic się nie zmienia, dopóki go nie potwierdzisz.” and `TextLink tone="muted"` „Użyj innego adresu”, which returns to the form. See Q-H16.
   6. Two-factor (design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:123-131):
      - `SectionTitle` with `Badge uppercase` tone success „Wł.” / neutral „Wył.”;
      - status paragraph `--type-sm` muted;
      - `Divider spacing="var(--sp-2)"` (4 px above and below);
      - `Method` e-mail; Divider 4 px; `Method` authenticator. `Method` is a grid of `20px minmax(0,1fr)`, column gap `--sp-4` (12 px): icon 20 px with `margin-top: 2px`; right column gap `--sp-4` with h3 `--type-h4` semibold + description `--type-sm` muted `margin-top: --sp-1` (2 px), FormField „Potwierdź hasłem” (password), and `Button variant="quiet"` („Włącz kody e-mail” / „Skonfiguruj”) disabled until a password is typed or while 2FA is on (design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:35-50);
      - when on: muted TextLink „Wyłącz weryfikację dwuskładnikową” (design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:130).

      No setup block, no activated view, no password for turning off. See Q-H17.
4. **Required by prompt-195, not in the kit:**
   - `LanguageChip` before the account menu (design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:63);
   - `AccountMenu` as a real popover. The kit reference is `AccountMenu`/`Popover`/`MenuItem` in design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:31-87: trigger 40 px with a 2 px `--surface-card` ring; `role="menu"` at `top: calc(100% + 8px)`, `right: 0`, `min-width: 224px`, padding 4 px, 1 px hairline, `--radius-lg` (20 px), `--shadow-lift`, gap 2 px; items 44 px, padding `0 --sp-4`, `--radius-sm`, `--type-body`, 18 px muted icon; desktop items „Profil”, „Konto”, rule, „Wyloguj”; phone adds „Polski” / „English” with flags between two rules (design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:10, 44, 54, 65-66, 74, 80-84);
   - `<header>` landmark before `<main>` and a skip link (design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:66);
   - focus rules of §3.3: focus to the first item, Escape and outside press return focus, arrow keys, reset `signOutFailed` on close (design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:70).
   - "Sections in one column of cards `--radius-card`" (design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:184). See Q-H14.

**Behaviour per viewer.** Signed in with a handle: logo and „Profil” → `/{handle}`. Signed in without a handle: logo and „Profil” → `/` → 307 `/onboarding`; the address form opens on `suggestHandle` (`page.tsx:68-70, 77-85`). Signed out → `/login` (`src/app/[locale]/(app)/layout.tsx:31`). The kit models only an account with a handle and 2FA off.

**Deleted / moved / kept.**

- Kept: `TOPBAR.settings.logo`, `TOPBAR.settings.account-menu`, `SETTINGS-ACCOUNT.address.current`, all `HANDLE-FORM.*` (settings mode), `SETTINGS-ACCOUNT.password.*`, `SETTINGS-ACCOUNT.email.new`, `.email.form-error`, `.email.submit`, `.email.sent`, all `SETTINGS-ACCOUNT.two-factor.*`.
- Added: the language chip in the bar, `<header>`, skip link.
- Under the kit's structure the following would change and are **not decided here**:
  - `.two-factor.app-key`, `.backup-codes`, `.app-code`, `.app-code-error`, `.app-activate`, `.activated-note`, `.done`, `.off-password`, `.off-error` have no kit counterpart (Q-H17);
  - `.email.sent` gains a "use another address" link (Q-H16);
  - `HANDLE-FORM.field.feedback` (verdicts), `.field.cooldown-note`, `.field.cooldown-ahead`, `.result.saved`, `.result.saved-redirect` have no kit counterpart, and the kit's success copy differs.
- e2e depends on `getByLabel("Nowy adres e-mail")`, the button „Wyślij link potwierdzający” and heading „Sprawdź obecną skrzynkę” (e2e/db/email-change.spec.ts:56-61). The other sections have no e2e (F-ACCOUNT-18).

**Findings.**

- Resolved per prompt-195: F-SHELL-4 and F-ACCOUNT-6 (chip in the settings bar), F-SHELL-8 (landmark + skip link), F-SHELL-10 and F-SHELL-13 (account menu reset and focus, design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:70, 192).
- Open: F-ACCOUNT-8 … F-ACCOUNT-18 (F-ACCOUNT-11 already fixed). The kit's "Użyj innego adresu" link would touch F-ACCOUNT-12. The kit's 2FA simplification would remove the surfaces of F-ACCOUNT-13, -14 and -15 without a stated decision.

**Open points.**

- O-BAR-1: on a phone, does the settings bar keep a separate `LanguageChip` before the account menu (design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:63), or put the language items inside the avatar menu as decision A6 does for `ProfileBar` (design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:14)? Today's settings bar does not collapse (D-SHELL-6).
- O-BAR-2: whether the avatar in this bar's menu takes `profiles.avatar_shape` (B5 names only the profile and work pages, design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:27).
- O-BAR-3: which measure the settings bar uses: `measure-page` today (`page.tsx:76`) or `measure-wide` in the kit `TopBar` (design/components/navigation/TopBar.jsx:33).
- O-SET-1: the kit's success lines are `StatusMessage` blocks (padded, tinted, with an icon) where today they are plain coloured lines. The spec's role rules (`role="status"` / `alert`) survive either way (design/components/feedback/StatusMessage.jsx:13-22). The design system's own note says a form uses the plain line (design/components/feedback/StatusMessage.prompt.md:8).

#### /settings/profile

**Layout.** None. A server-side 307 to `/settings/account` in the same locale; signed out, the `(app)` gate sends the visitor to `/login` first (`src/app/[locale]/(app)/settings/profile/page.tsx:11-20`; `src/app/[locale]/(app)/layout.tsx:31`). D-ACCOUNT-13.

**Reference.** `ProfileEditor.jsx` (design/ui_kits/app/ProfileEditor.jsx:1-145) draws a separate "LinkedIn-shaped" editor page:

- TopBar with Profile/Account tabs and a "View public profile" button (design/ui_kits/app/ProfileEditor.jsx:39-45);
- a `measure-page` grid `minmax(0,1fr) minmax(0,300px)` (design/ui_kits/app/ProfileEditor.jsx:46) holding a header card, a photo card with `PhotoUpload`, an address card with `HandleField`, an `EmptyState`, and a sticky aside with the plaque.

The app README maps it to `(app)/settings/profile/*` "(page, `avatar-section.tsx`, `display-name-form.tsx`)" (design/ui_kits/app/README.md:11). Neither of those two files exists in `src/app/[locale]/(app)/settings/profile/` (only `page.tsx`). The system readme says the editor "predates the panel-based editing and is kept for its forms" (design/readme.md:195). The 14.09 decisions put identity editing in the about panel (design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:38). The shot stage has no `profile` screen (design/ui_kits/app/shots.html:22-28), and the matrix has no shot of it (design/docs/handoff/shots/matrix.json:39-47). `PhotoUpload` and `EmptyState` are used on no other app-kit screen. The product's `empty-state.tsx` and `upload-progress.tsx` are not used on any route in this fragment.

**Deleted / moved / kept.** V-SETTINGS-PROFILE-REDIRECT kept as it is. e2e: "/settings/profile without a session lands on the login page" (docs/ui-specification.md:2800).

**Findings.** None.

**Open points.** None.

## 4. Dictionaries

### 4.1 Profile page and about panel

Scope: every string the profile page, its bar, its menus, the about panel (read-only and edit), the work card and the orbit tile show. Reference strings come from the `T` object in `design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:10` (pl) and `:11` (en), the `t` object in `design/components/profile/AboutPanel.jsx:137` (pl) and `:136` (en), and literals hard-coded in `ProfileBar.jsx`, `WorkCard.jsx`, `OrbitTile.jsx`, `Avatar.jsx`, `Plaque.jsx`, `PublicProfile.jsx` (menus) and `Hero.jsx` (`LanguageChip`). The compiled `design/_ds_bundle.js` carries the same `t`/`T` values (`design/_ds_bundle.js:1559-1599`, `:5092-5135`), so there is no second version to reconcile. None of these files contains a non-breaking space. Typographic characters inside string values: „ ” (Polish) and “ ” (English) inside `emptyBody`; the ellipsis character … in `addPlacePh` („Wpisz miejsce…” / "Type a place…", `design/components/profile/AboutPanel.jsx:136-137`); the middle dot · in the footer note (`design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:197`); the degree sign ° in the `OrbitTile` strings (`design/components/profile/OrbitTile.jsx:63`, `:90`, `:110`, `:115-116`, `:145`).

Product dictionaries: `messages/pl.json` and `messages/en.json` have the same 645-line layout, so one line number is valid for both files. Where a reference string is concatenated in code (`"Edytuj: " + work.name`), the literal part is quoted and the concatenation is written out; the product rule is A8, "all texts via dictionaries, no strings in components" (`SPEC.md:59`).

Every `Settings.profile.name.*`, `Settings.profile.avatar.*`, `Settings.profile.cover.*` and `Settings.profile.sections.*` key is read only by the owner's profile view (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/owner-profile-view.tsx`), with one exception: `Settings.profile.sections.counter` is also read by the work form (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/work-form.tsx:1636`, `:1665`). The settings page reads only `Settings.profile.handle.*` (`src/app/[locale]/(app)/settings/account/page.tsx:108`, `:118`, `:133`). None of the keys changed below is `counter`, so changing them changes only the profile.

These rows stay in the tables above even though a recorded contradiction touches them. Their key and literal text are the same whichever way the contradiction goes:
- `Shell.closePanel`: Q-E03 decides which control carries the label, not its text.
- „Anuluj” on the ×: the save model decides what × does, not its label.
- `Works.card.editNamed`: decision B4 sets the control's shape, not the name „Edytuj: {name}”.
- `Settings.profile.avatar.change`: the camera sits at the big avatar's bottom-right in `claude-code-prompt-195.md:127` and on the panel copy's bottom-left in decision C8 (`00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:41`); both label it „Zmień zdjęcie”.

### 4.2 The work's page, and the rest of the redesign (hero, 404, error screen, auth, onboarding, settings)

Scope of this part: every string of `WT` and every hard-coded string in `design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx`; the strings of `design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx`, `NotFound.jsx`; `design/ui_kits/app/Auth.jsx`, `Onboarding.jsx`, `AccountSettings.jsx`; the keys and copy named in `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md` (below "prompt-195") §3.2, §5, §6.5 and in `design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md` (below "decisions 14.09") A8/A9. The profile page and the about panel (`T` in `PublicProfile.jsx`, `t` in `AboutPanel.jsx`, the card, the bar) are in part A and are not repeated here.

Conventions used below:

- `messages/pl.json` and `messages/en.json` have the same key on the same line (both files are 645 lines, key for key). `messages/{pl,en}.json:N` means line N in both.
- Which reference files carry which languages: `WorkPage.jsx` `WT` — Polish and English (`design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:8-27`); `Hero.jsx` `HERO_T` — both (`design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx:6-9`); `NotFound.jsx` `NF_T` — both (`design/ui_kits/public-web/NotFound.jsx:5`); `AccountSettings.jsx` `ACC_T` — both (`design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:6-23`). **`Auth.jsx` and `Onboarding.jsx` are English only** (`design/ui_kits/app/Auth.jsx:3` — "All copy verbatim from messages/en.json"; `Onboarding.jsx` has no dictionary object). Where the reference has no Polish (or no English), the cell says "not in the reference".
- No string in any of these reference files, in `messages/*.json`, prompt-195 or decisions 14.09 contains a non-breaking space (searched for U+00A0, U+202F and `&nbsp;`). Quotes are copied as they are: Polish „ ”, English “ ” inside English strings, straight apostrophes (`card's`) where the source has them.
- "Name to be decided" = no document proposes a key; a suggested namespace follows in parentheses.
- Namespaces that exist today and are touched here: `Works`, `HomePage`, `NotFound`, `Login`, `Register`, `TwoFactor`, `Onboarding`, `HandleForm`, `Settings`, `Session`, `MobileMenu`, `LanguageSwitcher`, `AccountMenu`, `Footer`, `Brand`, `Metadata`. **`Shell` and `Error` do not exist today** (`messages/pl.json` has no such top-level key) and are created by the rows below. There is no `error.tsx` or `global-error.tsx` anywhere under `src/app` today.

#### 4.B1 The work's page — `V-WORK` (`/{handle}/{slug}`: read-only, `?edit=1`, new work)

The work's page replaces the in-place work form (`V-WORK-FORM`, `src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/work-form.tsx`) — prompt-195 §5.4 (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:177`). Its bar reuses `ProfileBar` and its "o nas" panel reuses `AboutPanel` read-only (`design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:178-179`); their strings (including the hard-coded bar toggle label „Otwórz panel: ” / „Zamknij panel: ” at `design/components/profile/ProfileBar.jsx:51`) are in part A. The orbit tile's own strings (`OrbitTile`, `design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:225,262`) are in the component part.

Bar controls (decisions 14.09 A8 and A9, `design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:16-17`): all owner controls are icon-only on every width, so each label below is an `aria-label` and also a `title` in the reference — pencil `aria-label={t.edit}` (`WorkPage.jsx:165`), trash `aria-label={t.delete}` (`WorkPage.jsx:159`, existing works only), × `aria-label={t.cancel}` (`WorkPage.jsx:160`), ✓ `aria-label={t.save}` (`WorkPage.jsx:161`). The pencil's label is plain „Edytuj” without the work's name (the card's pencil label `Works.card.editNamed` belongs to part A).

#### 4.B2 The rest of the redesign — skip link, hero, 404, error screen, auth, onboarding, settings

prompt-195 §6 keeps these screens' structure and re-skins them (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:179`); decisions 14.09 leave §6 untouched (`design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:50`). `Hero.jsx` and `AccountSettings.jsx` describe themselves as the product "as shipped (atlas 12.09.2026)" (`design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx:1`, `design/ui_kits/app/AccountSettings.jsx:1`). The auth, onboarding and settings kits nonetheless differ from today's dictionaries. prompt-195 approves the kit's look only for the profile and the work page (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:16`), and no document orders the kits' wording on the screens it keeps. So every row that comes from these kits, and both hero deletions (Q-I01), sit in this section's contested table. The rows left in "To add" come from prompt-195 itself.

## 5. E2E tests

### The database-backed project (`chromium-db`)

Scope: every file in `e2e/db/`, plus `playwright.config.ts` and `e2e/axe.ts`. Both Playwright projects run `Desktop Chrome` (`playwright.config.ts:90-108`), so every row below is about the desktop form unless a spec creates its own phone context (only `e2e/db/r360.spec.ts:372-378` does, with `devices["iPhone 13"]`).

How to read the tables:

- **One row per broken selector or assertion**, grouped by spec file. Each row has an ID (`HP-01`, …) so the "Certain vs likely" list after the tables can refer to it.
- "Selector / assertion today" is what the spec runs now; the product fact behind it is cited from `src/` or `messages/`.
- "What replaces it" names the role, accessible name or behaviour from the reference, with the file and line. Where the reference names nothing, the cell says so. Nothing here proposes a fix. Where sources disagree, the row points to section 6 (Contradictions).
- PR column uses the proposed split: **tokens / primitives / profile / work page + menu / re-skin**. "profile → work page + menu" means the old UI goes away in the profile PR and the test can only be rewritten once the work page exists (see contradiction Q-A03 about where the new-work flow lands).
- A row not listed under "Likely" is **certain**.

Some facts behind many rows:

- **The profile `<article>` card is gone** (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:84`). The only `<article>` elements on the new profile are work cards (`design/components/profile/WorkCard.jsx:102-110`).
- **The page's `h1` now lives inside the about panel** (`design/components/profile/AboutPanel.jsx:214`). The panel is `<aside aria-hidden={!open}>` (`AboutPanel.jsx:150-151`), so a role query only finds the `h1` while the panel is open. On desktop the panel is open on load (`design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:110`; `claude-code-prompt-195.md:113`). The name beside the page avatar is a `<p aria-hidden={about}>`, not a heading (`PublicProfile.jsx:178`).
- **The owner's pencil stays on screen while editing.** It is a round 40 px button, `aria-label` „Edytuj profil”, that becomes `disabled` at 50 % opacity during editing (`PublicProfile.jsx:138`; `design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:12`). Today the same bar button changes its label to „Zapisz” (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/owner-profile-view.tsx:591-603`). So `getByRole("button", { name: "Edytuj profil" })` still resolves, but `toBeVisible()` on it no longer proves that editing ended.
- **Identity „Zapisz” is a ✓ in the panel.** It is a 40 px black circle (`--action-solid`) with `aria-label` „Zapisz” in the panel's top-right corner (`AboutPanel.jsx:198-203`). It saves and leaves the panel open. The × (`aria-label` „Anuluj”, `AboutPanel.jsx:205`) cancels and closes the panel (`00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:39`; `PublicProfile.jsx:115-116`).
- **No work form on the profile.** A new work is the work page in edit mode with empty fields; an existing work is edited on `/{handle}/{slug}?edit=1`. Delete is in that page's bar (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:104,151,153,174,177`). The work page bar in edit mode holds only icons: trash `aria-label` „Usuń realizację” (existing works only), × „Anuluj”, ✓ „Zapisz”. The ✓ is disabled at 40 % until the work has a name and at least one photo or an orbit (`design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:153,159-161`; `00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:17`).
- **No lightbox on the profile.** Every picture on a card is a link to `/{handle}/{slug}`, with `aria-label` „Otwórz realizację: {name}” (`WorkCard.jsx:15-29,53,57`; `claude-code-prompt-195.md:88`; `00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:25`). The card's orbit gets no ring and no cue buttons (`WorkCard.jsx:55`; `design/components/profile/OrbitTile.jsx:16`). Its corner button is `arrow-up-right` „Otwórz realizację: {name}” (`OrbitTile.jsx:112-135`). The ring (desktop only), the cue buttons and „Powiększ widok 360°: {name}” exist on the work page (`WorkPage.jsx:262`; `OrbitTile.jsx:115,134,137-145`).
- **The about panel covers part of the works on desktop.** It is 380 px wide, `position: fixed; left: 0; z-index: 45` (`AboutPanel.jsx:128,153-158`; `PublicProfile.jsx:143,199`), and it "overlays the works — it does not push them" (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:113`). Raw `page.mouse` coordinates in the left 380 px of the column land on the panel.

#### Certain vs likely

Every row not listed below is **certain**: the reference, the decisions of 14.09 or prompt-195 name a different role, label, element or flow, and the selector cannot match it.

**Likely: depends on visual state, geometry, scroll position or timing**

- HP-03, AC-01, PS-10, PS-11: they assume the about panel is open when the assertion runs. It is open on desktop load (`PublicProfile.jsx:110`), but a collapse is remembered in `sessionStorage` under `a3d.about` (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:113`). The serial specs share one `page` (for example `profile-sections.spec.ts:30,35-46`), so one collapse hides the `h1` and the sections from role queries for every later test.
- HP-18, R3-02, AX-01: axe contrast over the gradient band, plus the token colours.
- WK-32, WK-33, LB-10, R3-13: axe runs that move to the work page, where the whole-document scan meets content the reference leaves undrawn (parameters, cue editor, inline reveal) and state the reference does not guard (a closed panel with focusable buttons, a button inside a slider).
- R3-01: `page.mouse` drag start under the 380 px panel.
- R3-07: raw mouse coordinates around the ring, under a fixed 64 px bar.
- R3-08: `requestAnimationFrame` stub and fixed waits.
- LB-06: bounding box of the reveal inside the new dialog.
- WO-04: pointer drag across tall stacked cards with an 80 px gap and edge auto-scroll.

**Likely: depends on something the reference leaves open (an id, a test id, an error slot, a request body) or on a recorded contradiction**

- HP-02 (wording of "drop the second log-in phrasing").
- HP-19 (whether the profile's own title, which already ends in the brand, goes through the new title template).
- HP-06, AU-01, AU-03 (file input ids).
- HP-09, WK-04, WK-05 (file input test ids).
- AU-02 (avatar assigned at once or on ✓, Q-E01).
- AU-04 (error line placement).

- LG-04 (menu items as links or buttons).
- LB-03, LB-05, LB-09 (reveal inline and/or in the dialog).
- PS-03 (option detail text), PS-04 (Q-E06), PS-06 (newlines in contentEditable), PS-07 (Q-E02), PS-08 (Q-E01), PS-12 (Q-E05).
- R3-06, R3-11 (Q-F05).
- WO-01, WO-02, WO-03 (Q-F10).

### The specs that run without a database (`e2e/*.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`) — 5.0 to 5.3

#### 5.0 Scope and the rules that decide whether a selector survives

- Files covered here: `e2e/a11y.spec.ts`, `e2e/avatar.spec.ts`, `e2e/axe.ts`, `e2e/global-setup.ts`, `e2e/handle.spec.ts`, `e2e/i18n.spec.ts`, `e2e/login.spec.ts`, `e2e/not-found.spec.ts`, `e2e/profile.spec.ts`, `e2e/register.spec.ts`, `e2e/reset-password.spec.ts`, `e2e/server-log.ts`, `e2e/settings.spec.ts`, `e2e/two-factor.spec.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`. The `e2e/db/**` specs are a separate fragment.
- They run in the Playwright project `chromium` (`playwright.config.ts:91-97`, `testIgnore: "**/db/**"`) against a server with no database. Both projects use the `Desktop Chrome` device only (`playwright.config.ts:96`, `:106`), whose viewport is 1280 × 720 (`node_modules/.pnpm/playwright-core@1.62.1/node_modules/playwright-core/lib/coreBundle.js:29070-29073`, in the main checkout). There is **no phone project**: every phone form of the redesign (breakpoint `sm` = 40rem = 640 px, `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:27`) needs a viewport below 640 px set per test.
- Playwright defaults that matter for the rows below: `getByRole(..., { name })` matches a case-insensitive **substring** unless `exact: true`; elements hidden from the accessibility tree (`display: none`, `aria-hidden`) are skipped; a locator that resolves to two elements fails any action or `expect` with a strict-mode violation; `toHaveTitle("text")` is a full match of the title.
- Axe scope: `e2e/axe.ts:19` runs only the tags `wcag2a`, `wcag2aa`, `wcag21a`, `wcag21aa`. In the installed axe-core 4.13.0 (`node_modules/.pnpm/axe-core@4.13.0/node_modules/axe-core/axe.js`, main checkout) the rules `landmark-one-main` (`:33111`), `page-has-heading-one` (`:33331`), `region` (`:33355`) and `skip-link` (`:33428`) are tagged `best-practice` and therefore **never run** here; `bypass` (`:32583`), `nested-interactive` (`:33262`) and `aria-hidden-focus` (`:32283`) are `wcag2a` and **do run**. "Landmarks" and "one h1" are therefore not guarded by axe today; they need explicit assertions (5.3).
- The specification's rule for this work: "A new UI that renames a role, an accessible name or a test id updates the specs named in the element's **Tests** line" (`docs/ui-specification.md:5631`).
- Pull request (PR) names used in the last column follow the proposed split: **tokens → primitives → profile → work page + menu → re-skin**.

#### 5.2 Certain vs likely

**Certain** — fail as soon as the change lands as the sources describe it: E1–E8 (title template), E9 (duplicate „Załóż konto”).

**Conditional on an open choice or a recorded contradiction** — fail only if the implementation takes one of two readings:
- E10 — relabel vs remove the hero's second button (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:62`; Q-I01).
- E11, E12, E13 — language list as `listbox`/`option` (reference) vs links in a `menu` (prompt-195, spec) (Q-C04).
- E20–E26 — auth screens re-skinned with structure kept vs the reference `TwoFactor` (Q-H08).
- E27 — whether the homepage keeps the layout's default title or gets a brand-only title of its own that the template then suffixes. The database-backed counterpart, where a title already ending in the brand could be suffixed again, is §5 database project HP-19.

**Depend on visual, geometry or timing assumptions** — the outcome depends on paint order, stacking and backgrounds or on compile timing, not on a label:
- E14, E15 — whether the bar text still has the scrim as an ancestor after the `<header>` move.
- E16 — contrast of the transparent bar over the cover band on a live profile.
- E19 — cold-compile timing of routes no longer warmed.

**Expected to pass but lose their subject, if the routing holds** — green, while no longer testing what their comments say: E17, E18. Whether the new `[handle]/[slug]` route answers these addresses is unverified (no build or run was allowed).

**Hold only if** (no row, listed so nobody breaks them by copying the kit):
- The home link „Wróć do domu” / "Back home" stays a **link** (`e2e/not-found.spec.ts:20-21`, `:39-42`; `e2e/profile.spec.ts:23-25`, `:56-58`), and so do the bar's „Zaloguj się” / „Załóż konto” (`e2e/login.spec.ts:139-140`). The reference renders these navigations as `<Button onClick>` (other navigations in the kit are `<a>`, e.g. the work page back link, `design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:181`) (`design/ui_kits/public-web/NotFound.jsx:19`; `design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx:74-75`, `:103-104`; `design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:126-127`).
- The hero photo stays at `/hero-facade-plaque.webp` (`e2e/login.spec.ts:145-148`; `src/app/[locale]/(public)/page.tsx:81`). The reference points at a kit asset `../../assets/hero-facade-plaque.jpeg` (`design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx:10`, `design/ui_kits/public-web/NotFound.jsx:13`).
- The chip trigger's accessible name stays exactly the locale name „Polski” (`e2e/i18n.spec.ts:38`; `design/ui_kits/public-web/Hero.jsx:36`).
- No new element on `/login` or `/en/login` gets a name containing „Zaloguj się” / "Log in" (substring match in `e2e/login.spec.ts:29`, `:45`, `:64`, `:73`, `:96`, `:108`, `:124`, `:129`, `:172`, `:179`, `:192`; `e2e/two-factor.spec.ts:30`). The auth-screen language chip (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:64`) is named „Polski” / "English", so it does not collide.

**Unaffected by the redesign** (read in full): `e2e/avatar.spec.ts` (API status only), `e2e/handle.spec.ts` (redirects, 401s, 404s of one-segment paths, `/register/verified` links), `e2e/profile.spec.ts` (404 body, `X-Robots-Tag`, reserved word), `e2e/server-log.ts`, `playwright.config.ts`. Also every line of `register.spec.ts`, `reset-password.spec.ts`, `settings.spec.ts`, `login.spec.ts`, `i18n.spec.ts`, `two-factor.spec.ts`, `a11y.spec.ts` not named in 5.1.

Photo tiles „Wymień”, „Usuń” (`:250-251`). Orbit „Wymień zip”, „Usuń widok 360°” (`:228-229`); without one, a 120 px tile „Dodaj zip R360” (`:121`, `:233`). No photos: a 260 px tile „Dodaj pierwsze zdjęcie” (`:121`, `:241`). A new work starts in edit mode, and × returns to the profile (`:134`, `:160`). ✓ creates the work and lands on `/{handle}/{slug}`; on an existing work it returns to the same address without `?edit=1` (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:104`, `:161`). The save sends the description, `card_layout`, `r360_autorotate` and the picture order (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:161`). Delete: the trash asks for a confirmation that names the R360 set, and success goes to `/{handle}` (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:153`). The kit deletes on the first press (`design/ui_kits/public-web/index.html:51`; Q-G06). Description limit: 300 in the kit (`WorkPage.jsx:11`, `:195`) and in `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:154`, 600 in `:100` of the same file (Q-G05). Photo limit: „Najwyżej dziesięć zdjęć.” (`WorkPage.jsx:14`) against three today (`src/db/schema.ts:390-394`) (Q-G04). Leave guard: T20. On the profile the „Realizacja” button with a plus shows only while the owner edits (`design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:184`; decisions B6 `00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:28`). Which pull request carries „+ Realizacja” and the new-work flow is recorded as Q-A03; what pressing it does to an open identity draft, as Q-F14. Owner empty-state copy „Wejdź w „Edytuj” i dodaj pierwszą plusem pod zdjęciem w tle. Nazwa i jedno zdjęcie wystarczą na start.” (`PublicProfile.jsx:10`, `:186-191`); today `e2e/db/works.spec.ts:768` checks only its title. Pointer drag-and-drop is geometry-dependent; the keyboard path is not. | work page + menu |

If it keeps happening, write to us."; button „Spróbuj ponownie” (`Error.retry`, calls `reset()`); the 404's home link; both languages; `global-error.tsx` works without the intl provider (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:185`). ## 6. Contradictions

Not resolved here — Dawid rules on them before the pull requests they block. **93 open**, of which **18 block work**; 2 already settled by Dawid and kept for the record. Every item quotes each side with `path:line`; each group ends with the suspected contradictions that were checked and rejected, and why. Precedence used when checking: decisions 14.09 over prompt-195; both over the UI specification for the target; the reference code for measurements — but where the reference code disagrees with a point a decision or prompt-195 states explicitly, the item stays open.

### A. Process: paths, language, PR order, issue scope (backend changes), precedence between documents

Issue #195 is not a file; it is cited as `issue #195 › <section>` (read with `gh issue view 195`).

#### Q-A01 — Order of the pull requests: three sequences

- **Sources:**
  - `design/docs/handoff/prompt-00-rozpoznanie.md:29` — „potwierdź lub popraw kolejność: tokens → prymitywy → profil → realizacja + menu → re-skin reszty”
  - `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:202-210` — „## 9. Delivery (as #195 proposes)” … „**Auth screens**” (:206), „**Onboarding + settings**” (:207), „**Profile**” (:208)
  - `issue #195 › Proposed delivery` — „3. The sign-in screens. 4. Onboarding and settings. 5. The profile page …”
- **What differs:** prompt-00 has no direction step, a separate primitives step, and puts the profile and the work page before the re-skin of auth, onboarding and settings. prompt-195 and the issue have seven steps with auth, onboarding and settings before the profile. The decisions of 14.09 say nothing about delivery order.
- **Affects:** section 7 (the PR split) and the order of every later prompt; **decide before:** tokens PR; **weight:** blocks work

- **What differs:** prompt-00 ships the menu with the work page (fourth step); prompt-195 and the issue ship menus, chip, bars and footer in the second pull request with the tokens. Decision A6 of 14.09 redefines the menus (phone menu with language, visitor hamburger) from the profile kit, after prompt-195's §9 was written.
- **Affects:** `AccountMenu`, `LanguageChip`, the visitor menu, `ProfileBar`, `C-FOOTER`, the skip link; **decide before:** tokens PR; **weight:** blocks work

The homepage menu icon is 18 px in the kit (`IconButton.jsx:33`) and 22 px in the product (`src/components/ui/mobile-menu.tsx:44`).

#### Q-B02 — Focus indicator: base.css outline or box-shadow ring
- **Sources:**
  - `design/tokens/base.css:7` — „outline:2px solid var(--focus-ring);outline-offset:2px”
  - `design/readme.md:150-151` — „Focus is a 2px ink outline at 2px offset, visible on every control (white on photographs).”
  - `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:33` — „in import order (`styles.css`): `fonts`, … `motion`, `base`” and „focus rings … are unchanged from what `globals.css` already has”
  - `docs/ui-specification.md:5207` — „applied as `focus-visible:shadow-[var(--ring-focus)]` with `outline-none`”
  - `src/components/ui/button.tsx:8` — „focus-visible:outline-none”; `:22` — „shadow-[var(--ring-focus)]”
- **What differs:** prompt-195 asks to port base.css, whose one rule draws an ink outline on every focused control with no photograph variant, and in the same paragraph keeps the product's box-shadow rings (`--ring-focus`, `--ring-focus-inverse`) drawn with the outline removed. Reference components rely on the outline; product components on the ring.
- **Affects:** the base.css port into `src/app/globals.css`; every control using `focus-visible:shadow-*`, including on-photo controls in ProfileBar and the hero; **decide before:** tokens; **weight:** changes a detail

#### Q-B03 — Input focus: ring plus border, or border colour only
- **Sources:**
  - `design/components/forms/Input.prompt.md:8` — „Focus is a 1px ink border plus the browser focus ring; no glow, no colour fill.”
  - `design/readme.md:151` — „visible on every control”
  - `design/components/forms/Input.jsx:39` — „outline: "none",” (border turns `--n-950` on focus, `:16-20`)
  - `docs/ui-specification.md:5175` — „focus: `--action-solid` border + focus-visible ring”
- **What differs:** The Input contract and the readme promise a focus ring on top of the ink border. The reference Input sets `outline: none` inline, which also cancels the base.css outline, so focus shows only as a 1 px border colour change. The product today draws both.
- **Affects:** Input (plain and prefixed, `Input.jsx:47-58`), Textarea; every auth, onboarding and settings form; work-page edit fields (`design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:189-192`); **decide before:** primitives; **weight:** changes a detail

#### Q-B04 — FormField: hint before or after the error line
- **Sources:**
  - `design/components/forms/FormField.d.ts:2` — „Label + control + hint + error, in that order, 4px apart.”
  - `design/components/forms/FormField.jsx:12-20` — error `<p role="alert">` (`:12`), then status (`:15`), then hint (`:18`)
  - `docs/ui-specification.md:5170` — „Does not set `aria-describedby` on the control (callers do); no error slot.”
- **What differs:** The contract places the hint above the error; the reference implementation renders the error or status line first and the hint last. The product's FormField has no error or status slot today (`src/components/ui/form-field.tsx:22`), so the target order can come only from these two disagreeing sources.
- **Affects:** FormField (gains error and status lines), the handle field's availability status, register, reset, settings and onboarding forms, work-page edit fields; **decide before:** primitives; **weight:** changes a detail

| globals.css lacks motion tokens prompt calls unchanged | `claude-code-prompt-195.md:33` lists `motion` among the files to port; `src/app/globals.css` has no motion tokens, so there is no competing value, only missing names (token table). |
| Colour transition on orbit cue buttons | `claude-code-prompt-195.md:146` keeps `ORBIT.cues.*` and `:194` does not overturn D-WORKS-18 (`docs/ui-specification.md:4268`); `design/readme.md:250-251` calls OrbitTile a stand-in and says the product keeps its own viewer. |
| Google Fonts kept versus SPEC §7 never list | `claude-code-prompt-195.md:23` and `:192` deliberately keep F-SHELL-18 open in its own issue; the redesign does not change font loading compared with today (`docs/ui-specification.md:5204`, `:5223`). |
| The one saturated colour: plaque versus auth medallion | Both describe the same state colour values (`design/tokens/colors.css:12`, `src/app/globals.css:61-64`); the medallion uses them (`src/app/[locale]/(auth)/register/verified/page.tsx:26`); only the wording differs. |

#### Q-C01 — Profile bar side padding on a phone: 12 or 16 px

- **Sources:**
  - `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:54` — „height **64 px desktop / 56 px phone**, side padding 24 / 16”
  - `design/components/profile/ProfileBar.jsx:36` — „padding: phone ? "0 var(--sp-4)" : "0 var(--sp-7)"”; logo layer `:54` — „left: phone ? "var(--sp-4)"”

- **Affects:** `ProfileBar` padding and logo offset, the phone gutter of `<main>` and the page avatar; **decide before:** work page; **weight:** changes a detail

#### Q-C07 — Footer note colour below the AA contrast threshold

- **Sources:**

  - `design/tokens/colors.css:15` — „--text-subtle:var(--n-500)”; `:4` — „--n-500:#6f7c85”

#### Q-C09 — About panel focus rules after the × and bar avatar are gone

#### Q-D01 — Monogram colours: white on --n-900 versus the stone palette
- **Sources:**
  - `design/components/core/Avatar.jsx:30` — „background: "var(--n-900)"” (line 31: „color: "var(--n-0)"”)

  - `src/lib/monogram.ts:14` — „MONOGRAM_BACKGROUND = "#e7e5e4"” (line 15: „#57534e”)
- **What differs:** The reference draws a missing photo as white initials on near-black and says this is the product's share-card monogram. prompt-195 keeps D-PROFILE-5, under which the avatar and the share card use one stone palette (#e7e5e4 ground, #57534e letters). The decisions of 14.09 do not mention the monogram.
- **Affects:** Avatar primitive (page avatar, panel copy, account menu), `src/lib/monogram.ts`, share card `src/app/api/og/[handle]/route.tsx`; **decide before:** primitives; **weight:** changes a detail

#### Q-D02 — Initials rule: kit first and last word versus product `initialsFrom`
- **Sources:**
  - `design/components/core/Avatar.jsx:4` — „split(/\s+/)” (line 6: „parts[0].slice(0, 2)”; line 7: „parts[0][0] + parts[parts.length - 1][0]”)
  - `src/lib/monogram.ts:30` — „.split(/[\s._+-]+/)” (line 35: „.slice(0, 2)”)
  - `docs/ui-specification.md:2860` — „first letter of each part, a leading digit/symbol skipped”
  - `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:116` — „the monogram rules D-PROFILE-5 unchanged”
- **What differs:** The reference splits on whitespace only, takes two characters from a single word, otherwise the first letters of the first and last words. The product splits on space, dot, underscore, plus and hyphen and takes the first letter of the first two parts, the same function the share card uses. "Studio" gives "ST" in the kit and "S" in the product; "Jan Maria Rokita" gives "JR" and "JM".
- **Affects:** Avatar primitive, `src/lib/monogram.ts`, `src/lib/monogram.test.ts`, share card route; **decide before:** primitives; **weight:** changes a detail

#### Q-F07 — Cover-thumbs layout with fewer than three photos

#### Q-J01 — Reference shots render in 1600×1000, not the stage size
- **Sources:**
  - `design/docs/handoff/shots/matrix.json:2` — „Viewport bierze się ze stage'a (desktop 1440×900, phone 390×844)”
  - `design/docs/handoff/README-eksport.md:46` — „Te same `id` są baseline’em dla testów wizualnych”

## 7. Proposed PR split

This section answers prompt-00 §7: "confirm or correct the order tokens → primitives → profile → work page + menu → re-skin of the rest; for each PR 3–6 small prompts, one component or one screen per prompt" (`design/docs/handoff/prompt-00-rozpoznanie.md:29`). It does not resolve any contradiction from section 6. Where a PR cannot start until Dawid rules on one, the PR says so and names the topic.

"PR" means a GitHub pull request. "Prompt" means one instruction to Claude Code, producing one component or one screen. "Gap map §n" points to the other sections of this document.

### 7.0 Rules every PR below follows

These come from the repository. They apply to every PR in 7.6, so they are not repeated there.

- **Preview label.** Add `preview` when the PR changes what a person sees. Never add it for docs, scripts, deploy or backend-only work (`CLAUDE.md:11-12`; `SPEC.md:394-396`).
- **Merging.** Branch protection on `main` requires the status check `ci-ok`. The branch must be up to date, merges are squash-only, and the rule binds admins too (`SPEC.md:340-346`). Before merging: `git rebase main`, push, wait for green, and resolve conflicts in the branch (`CLAUDE.md:13-14`).
- **Every merge deploys to dev.** Dev deploys automatically from `main` (`SPEC.md:328`), so an unfinished state between two PRs is live on dev until the next PR lands.
- **What CI runs.** On every pull request, `pr.yml` runs `pnpm check` plus a build. When code changes it also runs both Playwright projects: `chromium`, then `chromium-db` against a throwaway PostgreSQL (`SPEC.md:247-252`).
  - `pnpm check` is `typecheck && lint && test:coverage`. It does **not** build (`package.json:29`), so every prompt's check below names `pnpm build` separately.
- **Tests.** Deleting or skipping red tests without approval is forbidden (`SPEC.md:315`). A PR that removes a piece of UI must therefore rewrite the specs that drive it **in the same PR**. This rule shapes the order in 7.3.
- **Phone checks.** Both Playwright projects run `Desktop Chrome` only (`playwright.config.ts:90-107`, device at `:96` and `:106`). A phone check is either a per-test context below 640 px or a manual walk on the preview. "Phone and desktop" in a check below means both.
- **Migrations.**
  - Schema changes go only through migration files (G6, `SPEC.md:292`).
  - `pnpm db:seed` stays current (G7, `SPEC.md:293`).
  - A migration that only adds can be rolled back by redeploying an older image. One that drops, renames or tightens cannot (`SPEC.md:381-385`).
- **Backend changes.** Issue #195 says "No API or database change unless a view needs one, and the pull request then says so" (issue #195, section "What this is not"). Every PR below states "backend change" or "no backend change".
- **PR descriptions.** Record the overturned `D-*` decisions and the element fates (kept / moved / dropped) in the PR description (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:7`).
- **Per-PR bar from prompt-195.** Every PR needs `pnpm check`, `pnpm build`, both e2e projects green with selectors updated, axe clean on every view it touches, Polish and English checked by hand, and reduced motion checked once (`design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md:212`).
- **Before any code.** Every prompt starts by reading `CLAUDE.md` and the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (`CLAUDE.md:18-20`).

### 7.1 Three orderings in the sources (facts, not resolved)

| # | prompt-00 §7 (`prompt-00-rozpoznanie.md:29`) | prompt-195 §9 (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:202-212`) | issue #195, "Proposed delivery" |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | tokens | Direction: the prompt committed as `docs/ui-direction.md`, plus kit screenshots on the private atlas (`:204`) | The direction |
| 2 | primitives | Tokens + shared elements: bars, menus, chip, footer, skip link, plaque #199 (`:205`) | Tokens and the shared elements: top bars, menus, language switch, footer |
| 3 | profile | Auth screens + title template (`:206`) | The sign-in screens |
| 4 | work page + menu | Onboarding + settings (`:207`) | Onboarding and settings |
| 5 | re-skin of the rest | Profile: ProfileBar, cover, AboutPanel, identity edit, WorkCard, reorder with #173, empty state, new-work flow; migrations `works.slug`, `works.card_layout`, `works.r360_autorotate`, `works.description` (`:208`) | The profile page, viewing and editing |
| 6 | — | Works: the landing page, edit mode, lightbox ring rule, #159 (`:209`) | Works: gallery, lightbox, two-channel photo, orbit and the work form |
| 7 | — | 404 + error screen, leftovers, `docs/ui-specification.md` rewritten, new atlas screenshots (`:210`) | The 404 page and whatever is left |

Differences between the three, stated as facts:

1. **Menus, chip, bars and footer.** prompt-00 ships the menu with the work page. prompt-195 (`:205`) and the issue (item 2) ship them in the second PR, together with the tokens.
2. **Auth, onboarding and settings.** prompt-00 re-skins them last. prompt-195 (`:206-207`) and the issue (items 3–4) do them before the profile.
3. **The work card, the new-work flow and the four works columns.**
   - prompt-195 puts them in the profile PR (`:208`).
   - prompt-195 §5.3 makes a new work "this page in edit mode with nothing in it" (`:151`), and that page is delivered in its Works PR (`:209`).
   - The issue puts "gallery … and the work form" in the Works PR (item 6).
4. **`profiles.avatar_shape`.**
   - prompt-00 lists it among the migrations (`prompt-00-rozpoznanie.md:25`).
   - Decision B5 introduces it (`design/docs/handoff/00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:27`).
   - prompt-195's migration list for the profile PR does not contain it (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:208`).
5. **The 404 and the error screen.** prompt-195 (`:210`) and the issue (item 7) close with them; prompt-00 groups them under "re-skin of the rest".
6. **The direction step.**
   - prompt-195 asks for `docs/ui-direction.md` (`:204`); `docs/` holds no such file today.
   - The direction was exported as `design/docs/claude-code-prompt-195.md` (`design/docs/handoff/README-eksport.md:18`), and `design/` is on `main` (commit `a8032d3`, #204).
   - prompt-00 starts at tokens.
7. **Reference screenshots and "step 3".**
   - The handoff has a second prompt, `prompt-01-zrzuty.md`: 44 reference PNG files plus a report, committed under `design/docs/handoff/`, "Nic w `src/`" (nothing in `src/`) (`design/docs/handoff/prompt-01-zrzuty.md:13-15`).
   - The export readme calls those PNG files the baseline "dla testów wizualnych (krok 3)" (for visual tests, step 3) (`design/docs/handoff/README-eksport.md:46`).
   - No prompt or delivery list defines that step 3.
8. **Decisions of 14.09.** Section E lists what the decisions leave untouched (`00-decyzje-2026-09-14.md:50`). It does not mention prompt-195 §9 (delivery) either way.

**Contradictions touching this part (section 6):** Q-A01 — Order of the pull requests: three sequences; Q-A02 — Which pull request builds the menus, language chip, bars, footer; Q-A03 — New-work flow and work card placed before the work page exists; Q-A05 — Direction step: already approved, or still a first pull request

### 7.2 Dependencies found in sections 1–5 that decide the order

Each item names the fact and where it comes from. Gap map §1–§5 carry the detail.

**D1 — The tokens PR is visible on every screen.**
- `--radius-xs` … `--radius-2xl` are Tailwind's own radius keys, declared in `@theme` (`src/app/globals.css:73-78`).
- The 1:1 values double the small radii: xs 4 → 8, sm 6 → 12, md 8 → 16 px (`design/tokens/radius.css:5`).
- Every `rounded-xs/sm/md` in the product changes at once: 33 utilities in 21 files (gap map §1.1).
- That includes the `Card` that clips today's work-card pictures, which go from 8 to 16 px corners until the new card uses `--radius-picture` 8 px (`design/tokens/radius.css:6`).

The tokens PR is therefore a PR with a preview, not an invisible refactor.

**D2 — The tokens PR changes the plaque's weight unless the plaque changes with it.**
- The product plaque reads `var(--fw-regular)` and `var(--fw-medium)` (`src/components/ui/plaque.tsx:84`, `:104`).
- The design tokens set those to 450 and 550 (`design/tokens/typography.css:24-25`).
- Fira Sans Condensed is loaded only at 400 and 500 (gap map §1.3).
- The reference plaque uses literal 400 and 500 (`design/components/core/Plaque.jsx:57`, `:64`).

Either the tokens PR makes the product plaque's weights literal, or the plaque rebuild lands in the same PR.

**D3 — Later components read names the product does not have yet.**
- Bare `--n-*` names (gap map §1.4).
- The nine motion tokens (§1.5).
- `--measure-works` and `--radius-picture` (§1.1, §1.6).

Every primitive and screen that ports reference values reads them, so tokens come first.

**D4 — Icons gate every screen.**
- The icon name is a TypeScript union of 21 names (`src/components/ui/icon.tsx:6-27`), so a reference glyph missing from it fails `pnpm check`.
- 19 names the reference renders are missing, 13 of them on the profile, the work page and the menus (gap map §2 Icon).
- The reference loads glyphs as CSS masks from `unpkg.com` (`design/components/core/Icon.jsx:3`), a third-party host at run time.

Icons belong in the primitives PR, before any screen.

**D5 — The bar, the menus and the chip are shared by the profile and the work page.**
- The work page renders the same `ProfileBar` (`design/ui_kits/public-web/WorkPage.jsx:178`) as the profile (`design/ui_kits/public-web/PublicProfile.jsx:164`).
- The profile's right slot uses `LanguageChip` on desktop for every viewer (`PublicProfile.jsx:121`) and the account menu.
- The owner's menu already exists today on the profile and on settings (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/owner-profile-view.tsx:6`; `src/app/[locale]/(app)/settings/account/page.tsx:6`).
- The language chip is on the homepage and the visitor profile (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/page.tsx:6`; `src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/page.tsx:30`).

The menus therefore cannot wait for the work page. Whichever of the profile or the work page lands first needs them, and so do settings and onboarding. **This corrects prompt-00's "work page + menu".**

**D6 — The about panel is shared too.** The work page mounts `AboutPanel` read-only (`WorkPage.jsx:179`); the profile mounts it with editing (`PublicProfile.jsx:199`). The read-only panel can be built once, on whichever page comes first.

**D7 — Four works columns and one profiles column must exist before the new card or the work page.**
- `works` has no `slug`, `card_layout`, `r360_autorotate` or `description` (`src/db/schema.ts:268-308`).
- `profiles` has no `avatar_shape` (`src/db/schema.ts:185-217`).
- The last migration is `0019_works_position` (`drizzle/meta/_journal.json`, last entry), so the next is `0020`.
- The API side:
  - `PATCH /api/works/{id}` parses the whole `workInputSchema` (`src/app/api/works/[id]/route.ts:41-48`), which has none of the new fields (`src/lib/work-schemas.ts:24-88`).
  - `createWork` returns only `{ id }` (`src/lib/works.ts:332-335`, `:366`), so no redirect to `/{handle}/{slug}` is possible yet.
  - `POST /api/profile` accepts only `{ displayName }` (`src/app/api/profile/route.ts:16`).
- The e2e seed inserts works without a slug (`e2e/db/seed-works.ts:86-88`, `:104-106`) and returns `{ id, name }` only (`:11-14`).

The card links every picture to `/{handle}/{slug}` (`design/components/profile/WorkCard.jsx:53`, `:57`), and the work page looks a work up by slug. **Migrations therefore land before both.**

**D8 — The work page must exist before the profile drops its work form.**
- On the new profile, a card picture leads to the work page (`WorkCard.jsx:57`).
- „+ Realizacja” ("+ Work") opens the new-work page (`PublicProfile.jsx:184`).
- Deleting a work lives in the work page's bar (`WorkPage.jsx:159`).
- In the sources the old in-place form and its slot are dropped (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:174`, `:177`).

If the profile changes first, two things break:
- Owners on dev lose create, edit and delete until the work page lands.
- The e2e rows marked "profile → work page + menu" in gap map §5 (HP-08, LG-01, R3-03, R3-04, R3-05, R3-09, R3-10, R3-12, R3-13, WK-01, WK-25) could not be rewritten, because their target would not exist. Keeping CI green would then mean skipping tests, which `SPEC.md:315` forbids without approval.

**Hence the work page before the profile.** This corrects prompt-00's order and prompt-195's order alike.

**D9 — The leave guard sees links only.**
- The guard intercepts only `a[href]` clicks (`src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/use-leave-guard.ts:107-116`).
- The reference menu items are `<button role="menuitem">` (gap map §2 AccountMenu).
- `e2e/db/leave-guard.spec.ts:87-92` (row LG-04) breaks in whichever PR changes the menu items, and that is the menu PR, not the profile PR.

**D10 — axe on the new profile.**
- The profile band is a photo or a gradient under a transparent bar with white text (gap map §2 ProfileBar).
- The only undecided-contrast exception is for `landing-pl` and `landing-en` (`e2e/axe.ts:53-57`), and any other undecided contrast fails the run (`e2e/axe.ts:129-139`).
- Rows HP-18, R3-02, AX-01 and E16 therefore break in the PR that introduces the band.

**D11 — The work page may claim every two-segment address.** `src/app/[locale]/[...rest]/page.tsx:11-16` says two-segment addresses fall to the catch-all today. Once `[handle]/[slug]` exists, `e2e/not-found.spec.ts:14`, `:34` and the warm-up in `e2e/global-setup.ts:22-23` may be answered by the new route instead. No build or run confirmed it (rows E17–E19, unverified). If they are, E17 and E18 stay green but lose their subject, which T15 takes over.

**D12 — Other e2e breaks that follow a single change, not a screen.**
- The title template breaks rows E1–E8 (full-match titles), and HP-19 and E27 if a title that is, or already ends in, the brand gets the brand suffix again.
- The hero rename breaks E9, HP-01 and HP-02 (two links named „Załóż konto”, "Sign up").
- The language options as `role="option"` break E11–E13.

Each belongs to the PR that makes that one change.

**D13 — The plaque has three consumers.** `Plaque` is imported by `src/app/[locale]/(public)/[handle]/page.tsx:33`, `owner-profile-view.tsx:14` and `src/app/[locale]/(app)/onboarding/onboarding-steps.tsx:10`. Removing its `width` and `tilt` props (`src/components/ui/plaque.tsx:10-11`) is a compile error at all three, so the rebuild and its call sites are one prompt.

**D14 — The photo limit is a rule, not a view.**
- The kit's copy says ten photos (gap map §6, photo limit).
- A12 says 1–3.
- The database refuses a fourth position (`src/db/schema.ts:390-394`), and `WORK_PHOTOS_MAX = 3` (`src/lib/work-schemas.ts:12`).

Raising it is a SPEC change agreed with Dawid first (issue #195, "What this is not": "A screen that needs a rule changed is a SPEC change agreed with Dawid first"). Widening the CHECK is also not an additive migration in the sense of `SPEC.md:381-385`: an older image would meet works with more photos than it can show.

### 7.3 Recommendation

**prompt-00's order, corrected in three places:**

1. **The menus move forward.** Chip, popover, account menu, visitor menu, footer and skip link get their own "shell" PR right after the primitives (D5, D9). This matches prompt-195 `:205` and issue item 2 on *what*, but keeps them out of the tokens PR (D1: the tokens PR already changes every screen).
2. **A data PR comes before any works UI.** It is a backend change and says so (D7, D14).
3. **The work page comes before the profile** (D8). The profile splits into the works wall and the profile shell, so each PR carries one coherent set of e2e rewrites (gap map §5).

**Re-skins of sign-in, onboarding and settings move early, as in prompt-195 and the issue, not last as in prompt-00.** Reasons:
- They depend only on tokens, primitives and the shell (D5). Nothing in the works chain depends on them.
- The shell PR already edits the settings bar's account menu and the homepage menu.
- They close user-visible gaps that the contradiction-heavy works chain would otherwise hold back: no exit from onboarding (F-SHELL-6), no language switch for signed-in users (F-SHELL-4).
- They keep work flowing while Dawid rules on the many contradictions blocking PRs 6–10 (7.4).

The homepage copy, the 404 and the error screen stay last, as in prompt-195 `:210` and issue item 7. They depend on nothing after the shell and can move earlier without harm.

| PR | Title (as on GitHub) | Preview | Backend change | Depends on |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Reference screenshots of every kit state (#195) — optional, handoff prompt 01 | no | no | — |
| 1 | Design tokens ported 1:1 from the design system (#195) | yes | no | — |
| 2 | Primitives follow the design system: icons, buttons, fields, avatar shape, the growing plaque (#199, #195) | yes | no | 1 |
| 3 | One language chip and one menu shell on every bar, with a skip link (#195) | yes | no | 1, 2 |
| 4 | Sign-in screens re-skinned, with the language chip and page titles (#195) | yes | no | 1–3 |
| 5 | Onboarding and settings get a bar with the account menu and the language chip (#195) | yes | no | 1–3 |
| 6 | Works carry a slug, a card layout, a description and autorotate; profiles an avatar shape (#195) | no | **yes** | 1 |
| 7 | Every work has its own page at /{handle}/{slug} (#200, #159, #195) | yes | no (uses 6) | 1–3, 6 |
| 8 | A work is created, edited and deleted on its own page (#173, #195) | yes | no (uses 6) | 7 |
| 9 | The profile is a wall of work: one column of cards in three layouts (#195) | yes | no | 8 |
| 10 | The profile's identity lives in the about panel under a transparent bar (#195) | yes | no API or schema change; a server read of the signed-in viewer's own profile | 3, 6, 7, 9 |
| 11 | Homepage copy, the 404 and a new error screen (#195) | yes | no | 1–3 |
| 12 | The UI specification describes the new interface (#195) | no | no | 1–11 |

**Parallel work.**
- After PR 3, {4, 5, 11} are independent of the chain {6 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10}.
- Branches must be up to date and are squash-merged (`SPEC.md:340-346`), so a second branch rebases after each merge.
- Branches that add dictionary keys to `messages/pl.json` and `messages/en.json` will conflict there. Resolve in the branch (`CLAUDE.md:13-14`).

### 7.5 How section 5's PR column maps onto this split

Gap map §5 labels each broken selector with the split prompt-00 proposed. Rows T1–T22 are the one list of tests to write from scratch, gap map §5.3; the database-backed part of §5 points to it and keeps no list of its own. The recommended split sends each row here. Every row id appears once. Where a row spans views that land in different PRs, the PR named owns the test, and the other PRs keep it green under the per-PR bar in 7.0. ### 7.6 The pull requests

Each prompt lists what to read, what it produces and how it is checked:
- **Inputs:** `design/` files and gap map sections.
- **Output:** the files it changes.
- **Check:** the commands and walks that prove it.

Checks always include `pnpm check` and `pnpm build`; they are written once per prompt as "check + build".

#### PR 0 — Reference screenshots of every kit state (#195)

Optional. It exists because handoff prompt 01 does.

- **Scope:** `design/docs/handoff/prompt-01-zrzuty.md` as written: 44 PNG files under `design/docs/handoff/shots/out/` and a report `01-zrzuty-raport.md`. Nothing in `src/` (`prompt-01-zrzuty.md:13-15`).
- **Migrations and API:** no backend change.
- **Spec IDs and findings:** none.
- **e2e:** none.
- **Preview label:** no (docs).
- **Depends on:** nothing.
- **Risks:** the capture script renders in a 1600 × 1000 window, so `vh`-based band heights in the PNG files differ from a 1440 × 900 browser (gap map §3 profile, derived values).

Prompts:
1. **Capture.** Inputs: `prompt-01-zrzuty.md`, `design/docs/handoff/shots/matrix.json`, `README-eksport.md`. Output: `shots/out/*.png`. Check: 44 files, one per `id`.
2. **Report.** Inputs: the PNG files and gap map §6. Output: `01-zrzuty-raport.md` listing kit defects, not fixed. Check: every PNG opened once.
3. **Commit.** Inputs: the two outputs above. Output: a docs-only PR. Check: `ci-ok` green; no `src/` diff.

### 7.7 Why not the source orders as written

- **prompt-00 order (profile, then work page + menu).**
  - The profile would ship cards whose links, pencil, add button and delete lead to a page that does not exist yet (D8).
  - Its e2e rows marked "profile → work page + menu" could not be rewritten without skipping tests (`SPEC.md:315`).
  - The menus would arrive after the first screen that needs them (D5).
- **prompt-195 §9 and issue #195 (profile PR 5 before Works PR 6).**
  - Same D8 problem.
  - prompt-195 also puts the migrations and the "new-work flow" into the profile PR (`claude-code-prompt-195.md:208`), while its own §5.3 makes the new work the work page in edit mode (`:151`).
  - The issue moves the gallery and the work form into Works (item 6) but keeps the profile first.
- **Tokens and shared elements in one PR (prompt-195 `:205`, issue item 2).**
  - The token port alone changes every screen (D1) and the plaque's weight (D2).
  - The chip's options, the menu items and the header landmark each break a different e2e set (E11–E15, LG-04).
  - One PR would mix the widest visual change with the most behaviour changes. Splitting keeps each preview reviewable. This is a recommendation, not a dependency: merging PR 1–3 into one remains possible.
